reason: Corolla lip length compared with sepals, petals or tube is normal for a lip.
PATO_0000001 is the root 'quality' term and says nothing. The examples describe vein relief (impressed, flat, sunken), so use a specific relief or surface term.
Simple (unbranched) paraphyses are correct. The examples also describe the hairs of the paraphysis.
The examples are about glossy leaf surfaces and midribs, not trichomes. The pair exists only through a wrong part reading.

Lobe or sinus depth is meaningful, but the examples mix in unrelated dimensions (cordate sinus, forked length, 3-D sizes). A rule would need to separate depth words (deeply, shallowly) from numeric dimensions.
Porose describes the cell walls of moss leaves, not the leaf as a whole. A rule would need a cell wall or laminal cell bearer.
The examples are disarticulation of the spikelet at the rachilla or glumes. The PATO term 'diastatic' may not mean disarticulation. A rule would need a mapping to a deciduous/abscission term.
A papillose endostome (moss peristome) is a valid surface texture.
The examples mostly describe the hilum or the arrangement of seeds, not the orientation of the seed. A rule would need the actual bearer (hilum, embryo).
Narrow peristome teeth or segments are meaningful. 'Segments' may be a separate part.
A smooth gemma surface is meaningful. Some examples are about gemma cells.
A thin seed coat or testa is standard.
A smooth berry surface is standard.
Pseudobulb length is meaningful. Some examples are probably about other organs and need a check.
A persistent periderm means non-deciduous, which is correct.
Stigma lobe length is correct.
A woody thorn or spine is correct.

Presence or absence of the lobes themselves is fine, but some examples (glands, colleters on lobes) are about parts of the lobe. A rule would need to tell the lobe's own presence from the presence of a part on it.
A glabrous cypsela or its faces is correct.
Sepal-like (sepaloid) bracts are correct.
A D-shaped petiole in cross section is standard.
A glabrous corona lobe is meaningful. Some examples refer to a neighbouring part.
Petiole orientation (ascending, spreading) is meaningful.
Staminode size, often relative to fertile stamens, is correct.
A hyaline (transparent) leaf margin is a standard character.
A prismatic seed is correct. Some examples are cypselae, which is also fine.
A blunt leaf apex is correct.
An inflated seed or testa is meaningful. The crest example is a sub-part.
A linear labellum or lobe is correct.
Spreading spikes are correct.
Spike orientation (ascending, spreading, erect) is correct.
PATO_0001300 is a vague attribute. The examples are colours or hyaline scales, so use colour or transparency terms instead.
A winged leaf sheath is correct.
A glaucous or pruinose leaf lamina is correct. 'Not glaucous' needs negation handling.
Rudimentary (vestigial) stipules are correct.
A fimbriate corolla or corolla margin is correct.
Sessile or subsessile cymes are correct.
The examples are anther length, width or position, not depth. The pair exists only through a wrong reading.
A pyramidal tubercle is correct.
A cordate corolla lip or lip base is correct.
The number of stolons is a valid count.
Style branch length is correct. The 'staminal column' comparison is fine.
Pollen width as part of a size measurement is correct.
A terete bract is correct.
The orientation of a trichome or its arms is meaningful. 'Spreading to ascending' may belong to other parts.
An entire petal apex margin is correct.
A boat-shaped or prow-tipped leaf lamina is correct. It is really the apex, but the lamina is acceptable.
Alternate lobes are correct.
A labellum lobe colour is correct. Some examples describe the whole flower.
Dissected or subdivided lobes are correct.
Irregular peristome teeth are correct.
Calyptra colour is a standard moss character.
Obtuse and rounded are different shapes, and the quality really describes the apex of the nut. A rule would need to map 'rounded' elsewhere and use an apex bearer.
The examples are about leaf veins, not vascular bundles, so the part may be wrong. A rule would need to map 'veins' to a vein or venation part.
Opposite lobes are correct.
Slender shoots are meaningful.
Ligulate bracts map to strap-shaped, which is acceptable.
The 2-D shape of a megasporophyll (flabellate, orbicular) is correct, as in cycads.
A glandular leaf rachis is correct.
Large or larger lobes are correct.
